text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Sharp warnings to Sarajevo, Belgrade and Zagreb to fulfill international obligations before the European Union summit in Amsterdam.
- Sixth week of medics' strike begins with closing of biggest out-patients clinic in Belgrade.
- Schools may not reopen on September 1 unless late wages paid to teachers by then, warns Serbian education trade union.

- Former Yugoslav Prime Minister and U.S. business magnate Milan Panic would beat Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic in elections for the president of Yugoslavia, according to an Institute of Social Sciences poll.
- Socialist Party of Serbia Vice President Milorad Vucelic says 100 million German marks will be set aside from the sale of Serbia's Telekom for the pension fund and public works.

- Yugoslav parliament to discuss 41-point agenda at extraordinary session on June 26, including laws on customs, taxes, foreign currency operations, payment operations. Several laws implemented during sanctions to be abolished or amended.
- Opposition parties in Montenegro call for urgent debate on proposals for changes to the Yugoslav constitution and the Serbian president's candidacy for president of Yugoslavia.
- Under final version of draft Serbian privatisation law, free shares for workers will be worth 400 German marks for each year of service.
- McDonalds will have 13 restaurants in Yugoslavia by the end of this year, 22 by the end of 1998, says director of Geneks McDonalds Dragoljub Jakic.

- Slovenian central bank governor France Arhar says Slovenia, Croatia and Macedonia soon to invite National Bank of Yugoslavia governor to a meeting of central bank governors of all former Yugoslav states.
- The crisis in Bosnia could escalate soon, former high representative for Bosnia Carl Bildt says in talks with the Serbian president.
- Yugoslav industrial output in May drops 2.4 percent against April, up 9.3 percent on May last year.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia, Italy to sign agreement on cooperation in culture and arts.
- Yugoslav bankers discuss advancing payment operations in Moscow. Yugoslav-Russian Veksim bank has secured six regular correspondent accounts with European banks.
- Money supply has grown to 5.8 billion dinars and pressure to expand it even further is increasing, says Yugoslav central bank research centre director Jovan Petrovic.
- Komercijalna banka A.D. says lasting capital raised by 40 million dinars, to invest $1.5 million in Veksim bank of Moscow, founded by Jugobanka A.D. of Belgrade.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- Parliament approved 1997 programme guideline for state-owned media, passed government proposal that TV Montenegro executive board convene on Friday to discuss the responsibility of editor-in-chief Vladislav Asanin.

- According to a poll conducted by Belgrade's Partner Marketing, 41.1 percent believe Montenegro would best be represented by incumbent Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, 22.6 percent by republican President Momir Bulatovic.

- Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) local Niksic branch unanimously requests that next session of the party's Main Board establish the responsibility of party president Momir Bulatovic, who is by statute responsible for party unity, for conflicts within the republic's ruling party. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
